headline: Adjusted EPS rises, GAAP flat, full-year guidance affirmed
summary_short: Exelon posted Q2 2026 GAAP EPS of $0.39, flat y/y, while Adjusted (non-GAAP) operating EPS rose to $0.43 from $0.39 a year ago on higher distribution/transmission rates across ComEd, BGE and PHI. Revenue of $5,967M was up 9.9% y/y but down 17.6% q/q on normal seasonal (winter-to-summer) load patterns.
summary_long: Q2 2026 GAAP net income was $396M ($0.39/share), essentially flat y/y; Adjusted (non-GAAP) operating earnings rose to $438M ($0.43/share) from $392M ($0.39/share) a year ago. The gain reflects higher distribution and transmission rates at ComEd and PHI, distribution rates at BGE, the absence of PECO surcharge credits, higher AFUDC at ComEd, and favorable PECO weather — partly offset by higher depreciation at PECO/PHI, higher BGE credit-loss expense, and higher PECO interest expense and taxes. Cash rose to $1,813M from $626M at year-end on debt issuance (ComEd $1,425M, BGE $925M, Pepco $130M). Exelon affirmed FY2026 adjusted operating EPS guidance of $2.81-$2.91 and reaffirmed EPS CAGR near the top end of 5-7% (2025-2029), and declared a $0.42/share quarterly dividend.

drivers.explanation: CFO Jeanne Jones said Q2 adjusted operating EPS of $0.43 was in line with expectations discussed on the Q1 call, keeping Exelon on track for full-year EPS of $2.81-$2.91 and top-end 5-7% annualized growth through 2029.

Y/y growth tracks the release's stated earnings drivers: higher ComEd/PHI distribution and transmission rates, higher BGE distribution rates, and absence of PECO surcharge credits; the q/q decline is normal seasonal load (Q1 winter heating demand vs. Q2).
Not itself a labeled release metric; y/y growth is consistent with the rate-driven revenue increase outpacing the rise in purchased power and fuel costs.
Tracks the same rate increases and PECO surcharge-credit absence cited for revenue, net of higher operating and maintenance and depreciation expense; not broken out separately by the release.
Follows the operating-income drivers above; not a labeled release metric.
Follows the operating-income increase plus the depreciation and amortization addback disclosed in the consolidating statement of operations.

The release attributes the y/y increase to higher utility earnings from ComEd/PHI/BGE rate increases, PECO surcharge-credit absence, and favorable PECO weather, partly offset by higher PECO/PHI depreciation, BGE credit losses, and PECO interest expense and taxes.
The release states GAAP net income per share 'remained relatively consistent with the prior period' at $0.39, holding basic EPS flat y/y despite the underlying net-income drivers above.
Mirrors the basic EPS result above on the same flat net-income comparison and a stable diluted share count.
